🚫 Your SQL query looks fine... but is it secretly costing you time and compute? 💸
I just dropped a deep-dive PDF guide breaking down one of the most commonly misunderstood performance questions in SQL:
🔍 EXISTS vs IN – Which One Should You Use?
✨ Real-world examples
✨ Interview tips
✨ Performance tuning across engines like Spark, BigQuery & Synapse
✨ How NULLs can break your logic silently
✨ When to use LEFT SEMI JOIN in Spark instead
📌 This isn’t just theory. I’ve seen this mistake tank query performance in real production pipelines — and it's a favorite interview question at companies like Oracle and Capgemini , Accenture.
✅ TL;DR:
Use EXISTS when working with large, dynamic, or NULL-prone datasets.
Use IN only when you're sure the list is small, static, and clean.
📥 Download the PDF below if you're a Data Engineer, Analyst, or SQL learner who wants to stop guessing and start optimizing.
👇 Drop a "SQL 🔥" in the comments if you’d like a version with query plan visuals too!
